content.title: About
content.content: Reduced‑fat evaporated milk (2 %) is a dairy product made by removing most of the water from regular milk and adding a modest amount of sugar. It retains most of milk’s nutrients while offering lower calories and fat compared with traditional sweetened condensed milk.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Evaporated milk was invented in the 19th century as a way to preserve milk without refrigeration.
The reduced‑fat version appeared later as consumers sought lighter alternatives.
Typical sugar content in sweetened versions is about 55 % of the product’s weight.
Its thick texture makes it popular in desserts, confectionery, and beverages.
In many countries evaporated milk is a traditional ingredient for holiday cakes and puddings.

items.title: Rich in calcium
items.content: Evaporated milk provides a high amount of calcium, essential for strong bones and teeth.

items.title: Source of protein
items.content: Despite the low fat, it still supplies about 7 g of protein per 100 g, supporting muscle maintenance.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: It contains riboflavin (B2) and vitamin B12, which are important for energy metabolism.

items.title: Low fat content
items.content: With only 2 % fat, it fits better into calorie‑controlled diets.

items.title: Adds creaminess without extra fat
items.content: Its dense consistency allows it to give a creamy mouthfeel to dishes without needing additional butter or oil.

items.title: High sugar content
items.content: The added sugar can raise blood glucose levels and increase the risk of dental caries.

items.title: Lactose intolerance
items.content: The product contains lactose, so those who are intolerant should choose lactose‑free alternatives.

items.title: Milk protein allergy
items.content: People allergic to casein or whey may experience reactions.

items.title: Caloric density
items.content: Even with reduced fat, the sugar makes it relatively calorie‑dense.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Reduced‑fat evaporated milk is used in baking, custards, ice cream, sweet sauces, and beverages. It can be reconstituted with water or added to coffee for a sweet, low‑fat flavor.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the unopened can in a cool, dry place. After opening, store in the refrigerator and use within 2–3 weeks. Discard if it develops a sour smell or off‑color.
